rows.title: Acidität begründen
rows.description: Die lernende Person kann die Acidität von Alkohol-Molekülen und Carbonsäure-Molekülen vergleichen und den Einfluss polarer Bindungen, induktiver Effekte und Mesomerie auf die Säurestärke von Carbonsäuren erklären.
rows.descriptionEn: The learner can compare the acidity of alcohol molecules and carboxylic acid molecules and explain the influence of polar bonds, inductive effects, and resonance on the acid strength of carboxylic acids.
rows.sourceBasis: Actual HE Q1.3#B02A01 plus both current BY C10 acidity occurrences. Resonance belongs to both HE GK and LK, not only LK.
scientificImageConstraints: Compare an alcohol and a carboxylic acid in the same aqueous conditions, not acid versus neutral pH as a universal substitute for acid strength.
Depict the conjugate carboxylate as one delocalized ion; resonance structures are representations, not separate species interconverting.
If a substituent example is shown, distinguish its inductive effect from carboxylate resonance and use a genuinely electron-withdrawing substituent.
No quantitative pKa recall quota; no scientifically false moving proton between the two carboxylate oxygen atoms.

rows.title: Seifen herstellen
rows.description: Die lernende Person kann die alkalische Hydrolyse von Fetten zur Herstellung von Seife durchführen, die Bildung von Glycerin und Fettsäuresalzen anhand der Esterstruktur erklären und die Seife durch Aussalzen von der wässrigen Phase trennen.
rows.descriptionEn: The learner can carry out the alkaline hydrolysis of fats to prepare soap, explain the formation of glycerol and fatty acid salts using the ester structure, and separate the soap from the aqueous phase by salting out.
rows.sourceBasis: Actual HE Q1.4#B01A01 and HB fats/soap context. Lab performance is an actual required performance, not supplied-data completion.
scientificImageConstraints: Fat is a triacylglycerol; hydroxide-driven hydrolysis yields glycerol and fatty-acid carboxylate salts, not free fatty acids as the direct alkaline products.
Saponification equation is triacylglycerol plus three NaOH to glycerol plus three sodium carboxylates; no equilibrium double arrow for the net alkaline process.
Salting out separates soap from the aqueous phase; glycerol remains in that aqueous phase.
Conceptual school-lab schematic, no DIY recipe or home-food-use instruction.

rows.title: Redoxbasierte Konservierung
rows.description: Die lernende Person kann redoxaktive Konservierungsstrategien am Beispiel von Ascorbinsäure anhand bereitgestellter Reaktions- und Vergleichsdaten bewerten und dabei antioxidative Wirkung von antimikrobieller Konservierung unterscheiden.
rows.descriptionEn: The learner can evaluate redox-active preservation strategies using ascorbic acid as an example and supplied reaction and comparison data, and distinguish antioxidant action from antimicrobial preservation.
rows.sourceBasis: Own contextual transfer operationalization of actual HE Q1.5 ascorbic acid antioxidant and preservation context, not an official HE bullet literally requiring a separate redox-preservation module. This boundary requires independent source acceptance before operative adoption.
scientificImageConstraints: Show antioxidant electron donation: ascorbic acid is oxidized while a supplied oxidant is reduced; not antimicrobe shielding or general bacterial destruction.
If chemical equations are displayed, use ascorbic acid to dehydroascorbic acid plus two protons and two electrons under stated conditions, or leave electron transfer qualitative.
No guarantee of edibility, sterility or unchanged nutrient content; antioxidant action can slow selected oxidation while microorganisms may remain.
Any comparison must represent the same supplied chemical oxidation conditions with and without antioxidant; no universal shelf-life claim.
